title: RCMP watchdog launches Taser investigation
article: The RCMP's watchdog will examine the conduct of officers who participated in incidents-or were present-when individuals in custody died after being Tasered.
A focus of the investigation will be whether officers acted in compliance with training, policy, procedures and guidelines in their use the weapons.
The probe will also consider whether existing RCMP policies, procedures and guidelines relating to the use of Tasers are adequate.
Saulnier died July 15, 2005 while being restrained by Digby RCMP officers.
Nova Scotia's chief medical examiner found that Saulnier, 42, died of cardiac arrest due to excited delirium.
Saulnier's family launched a lawsuit against the Attorney General of Canada representing the Royal Canadian Mounted Police in 2007.
The suit alleges the officers' use of an inappropriate and dangerous hold contributed to Saulnier's death.
The suit also alleges that although RCMP officers involved acted within the scope of their duties, the Taser was used "in an inappropriate, ineffective, and dangerous manner."

In documents obtained from Jamie MacGillvray, the Saulnier family's lawyer, illustrations of injuries to Paul Saulnier include "35 small shallow irregularly shaped abrasions on his back...some containing small amounts of eschar (slough produced by a thermal burn.)."
MacGillvray says Saulnier lay face down in a 'hogtie' restraint while he was shocked repeatedly with a Taser in stun mode.
